question: The value of \(\left(\frac{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + x\right) + \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + x\right)}{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right) - \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}\right)^2\) is
working: Numerator = -sin x + cos x, denominator = sin x - cos x, so the ratio is exactly -1 and its square is 1. Sympy simplify returns 1 and numeric checks at x = 0.3, 1.1, 2.0 all give 1.000000.

question: The value of \(\left(1 + \cos\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\left(1 + \cos\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\left(1 + \cos\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\left(1 + \cos\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\) is
working: Pair the supplementary cosines: (1+√3/2)(1-√3/2) = 1/4 and (1+1/2)(1-1/2) = 3/4, product 3/16. Sympy simplify of the full product returns exactly 3/16.

question: \(\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 + 2\cos4\theta}}\) is
working: 2 + 2cos4θ = 4cos² 2θ so the inner root is 2cos2θ, then 2 + 2cos2θ = 4cos²θ giving 2cosθ. Numeric check at θ = 0.1/0.3/0.5 gives 1.99001/1.91067/1.75517 matching 2cosθ exactly (2cos2θ gives 1.96013/1.65067/1.08060).

question: The number of values of \(\theta \in (-\pi, \pi)\) satisfying \(\sin 5\theta \cos 3\theta = \sin 6\theta \cos 2\theta\) is
working: Product-to-sum reduces both sides to (sin8θ + sin2θ)/2 = (sin8θ + sin4θ)/2, i.e. sin4θ = sin2θ ⇒ 2cos3θ sinθ = 0. A 2-million-point sign-change scan of (-π, π) found exactly 7 roots: θ/π = 0, ±1/6, ±1/2, ±5/6.

question: \(2\sin^2\theta + \sqrt{3}\cos\theta + 1 = 0\). Then \(\theta =\)
working: Substituting sin² = 1 - cos² gives 2cos²θ - √3 cosθ - 3 = 0, whose roots are cosθ = √3 (rejected) and cosθ = -√3/2. Sympy solveset on [0, 2π] returns {5π/6, 7π/6}; only 5π/6 is offered.

question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio \(1 : 2 : 3\), then the corresponding sides are in the ratio
working: Angles are 30°, 60°, 90°; by the sine rule sides are proportional to sin30 : sin60 : sin90 = 1/2 : √3/2 : 1 = 1 : √3 : 2.

question: In any triangle \(ABC\), \(c^2\sin 2B + b^2\sin 2C\) is equal to
working: Writing b = 2R sinB, c = 2R sinC gives 8R² sinB sinC sin(B+C) = 8R² sinA sinB sinC, while Δ = 2R² sinA sinB sinC, so the ratio is 4. Numeric check on four random triangles (A,B) = (0.7,0.9), (1.2,0.5), (0.4,1.9), (π/3,π/3) gave LHS/Δ = 4.000000 every time.

question: The period of \(\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x\) is
working: sin⁴x + cos⁴x = 1 - ½ sin² 2x = 3/4 + (cos4x)/4, whose period is 2π/4 = π/2. Numeric shift test: max|f(t)-f(t+π/2)| = 7.8e-16 while max|f(t)-f(t+π/4)| = 0.5.

question: \(\sin(\cot^{-1}x) = \)
working: cot⁻¹x lies in (0, π) where sine is positive, and cotθ = x gives sinθ = 1/√(1+x²). Numeric check at x = -3, -0.5, 0.5, 3 matched 1/√(1+x²) to 15 digits, including the negative x values where option B would fail.

question: Find \(\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\)
working: cos⁻¹(4/5) = tan⁻¹(3/4), and tan⁻¹(3/4)+tan⁻¹(3/5) = tan⁻¹((27/20)/(11/20)) = tan⁻¹(27/11) since the product 9/20 < 1. Numerically the LHS is 1.18392061 and atan(27/11) = 1.18392061 (atan(0.7) = 0.6107, so A is far off; option C is invalid as 7/5 > 1).

question: The area of the triangle whose vertices are the points \((a(a+1),\ a+1)\), \(((a+1)(a+2),\ a+2)\) and \(((a+2)(a+3),\ a+3)\) is equal to
working: Edge vectors from the first vertex are (2a+2, 1) and (4a+6, 2), whose cross product is 2(2a+2) - (4a+6) = -2 independent of a, so the area is |-2|/2 = 1. Sympy simplification of the shoelace expression returns exactly 1 (a negative area, option A, is impossible).

question: If the distance between \((2, 3)\) and \((-5, 2)\) is equal to the distance between \((x, 2)\) and \((1, 3)\), then the values of \(x\) are
working: First distance is √(49+1) = √50; setting (x-1)² + 1 = 50 gives (x-1)² = 49, so x - 1 = ±7 and x = 8 or x = -6.

question: The slope of the straight line \(\frac{x}{10} - \frac{y}{4} = 3\) is
working: Solving for y: y = 4x/10 - 12 = (2/5)x - 12, so the slope is 2/5. Equivalently -A/B = -(1/10)/(-1/4) = 2/5.

question: A straight line meets the coordinate axes at \(A\) and \(B\), so that the centroid of the triangle \(OAB\) is \((1, 2)\). Then the equation of the line \(AB\) is
working: With A = (p,0), B = (0,q), the centroid of OAB is (p/3, q/3) = (1,2), giving p = 3 and q = 6. The intercept form x/3 + y/6 = 1 clears to 2x + y = 6, which indeed passes through (3,0) and (0,6).

question: If the vector \(8\hat{i} + a\hat{j}\) of magnitude 10 is in the direction of the vector \(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}\), then the value of \(a\) is equal to
working: The unit vector along 4i - 3j is (4i - 3j)/5, so a vector of magnitude 10 in that direction is 8i - 6j, giving a = -6. Consistency check: |8i - 6j| = √(64+36) = 10 and 8/4 = -6/-3 = 2, so it is genuinely parallel (not anti-parallel).

question: If \( |\vec{P} - \vec{Q}| = |\vec{Q}| \) and \( |\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}| = |\vec{P} \cdot \vec{Q}| \), then
working: The first condition expands to |P|² = 2|P||Q|cosθ, so cosθ > 0; the second gives sinθ = |cosθ|, hence θ = 45° — neither parallel (0°) nor perpendicular, and P·Q ≠ 0. Verified with Q = (1,0,0) and P = √2·(cos45°, sin45°, 0): |P-Q| = |Q| = 1 and |P×Q| = |P·Q| = 1. Marked medium only because the degenerate P = 0 case technically also satisfies both, but 45° is the intended non-trivial answer and none of A/B/C fits it.
